Memory hook: 'Sa Church May Tribunal at Eskwela.' The plaza complex physically expressed centralized colonial authority — the church anchored religious power, the municipio anchored civil authority, the marketplace anchored economic life. Streets radiated from the plaza in a gridiron (quadícula) pattern, with eight streets exiting from the four corners.
